wordmark.purpose: WORLDCONS on the strap; the same voice sets a con's short name on its no-image art plate (24px, uppercase).

display.purpose: Con page title, the Guests wall heading and page titles; 24px on phones.

display-month.purpose: Month headings over the badge grid, with the con count beside them; 24px on phones.

headline.purpose: A guest's name on their own credential, and empty-state headings (800-850).

title.purpose: Con names on badges, clamped to three balanced lines.

title-sm.purpose: Credential names, wall section heads, result counts; ruler months in uppercase at 112% width.

body.purpose: Running text and place lines; tabular numerals inherit everywhere from here.

label.purpose: Every control label; buttons and badge date lines run at 650.

label-ribbon.purpose: Satin ribbons, type toggles and day boxes, uppercase.

label-band.purpose: The ink role band at the foot of a credential, uppercase.

meta.purpose: Day counts, face-strip captions, other-con counts, known-for lines and countdown chips.

shadows.name: laminate-rest
shadows.purpose: Badges, credentials, Other-dates links and the empty-wall card at rest (light theme).

shadows.name: laminate-rest-dark
shadows.purpose: Laminate rest on the charcoal hall.

shadows.name: laminate-lift
shadows.purpose: Hovered badge or credential (with a 3px rise) and the three popovers: the suggestion panel, the place picker panel and the toast (light theme).

shadows.name: laminate-lift-dark
shadows.purpose: Laminate lift on the charcoal hall.

shadows.name: punch
shadows.purpose: The lanyard slot cut through to the hall; 0.25 for the corner punch on an ended con.

shadows.name: ribbon-fold
shadows.purpose: Top edge of a hanging ribbon where it tucks under the badge; 0.35 on a pressed type toggle.

shadows.name: art-hairline
shadows.purpose: Edge on the key-art window so pale logo plates do not melt into the white badge.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every transition and keyframe.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hover rise of 3px into the lift shadow.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons rise 1px on hover and settle on press.

motion.name: chevron-turn
motion.purpose: A place picker chevron turns over while its panel is open.

motion.name: tint
motion.purpose: Search field fill, type-toggle tint, clip icon fade.

motion.name: swing
motion.purpose: A badge swings from its slot when clipped to the lanyard.

motion.name: bump
motion.purpose: The lanyard count disc on the strap whenever a con is clipped or removed (including undo).

motion.name: sheet-in
motion.purpose: The phone filter sheet rising into thumb reach.

motion.name: toast
motion.purpose: Toast rising into place at the bottom centre.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Skeleton art and text bars while the list loads.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition.

components.name: Satin Ribbons
components.description: The ten con-type ribbons: flat satin colour, notched 7px tail, fold shadow at the top, 12px/800 uppercase label at 4.5:1 or better. Keyboard focus is an inset 2px ring in the label ink, because the notch clips anything outside the shape.

components.name: Type Ribbon Toggles
components.description: Con-type filters drawn as the badge ribbon: 15% tint with a 3px satin top band at rest, 26% and a 1px drop on hover, full satin colour with the fold shadow when pressed.

narrative.overview:
WorldCons is a convention hall seen from the badge-pickup desk. A cool grey ground, a black strap across the top that carries the wordmark, and every convention hanging in the hall as a white laminated badge: a punched lanyard slot, inset key art, a heavy wide-set name, a tabular date line, a strip of guest faces. Con types are satin ribbons hanging from each badge's bottom edge. Guests wear 4:5 photo credentials in the same laminate, with their role printed in an ink band at the foot. Clipping a con to your lanyard is the one personal act, and the badge swings on its slot when you do it.

The hierarchy works like a type specimen: one family (Archivo), one ink, and every level separated by size, weight and the width axis, never by colour. Colour lives in exactly two places: the photographs and key art (faces are the headline, so a guest is never a bare name) and the ten flat satin ribbon colours. Ink is the only action colour, and pressing anything fills it with ink. Density is generous for a directory: four badges across at desktop width, roomy rows so the ribbons can hang, and names that never overflow.

Confirmed rejections: the Eventbrite card with a pin icon and a filter sidebar; the dark gamer-neon default and the glassy, holographic neon-dark look the owner has already turned down; the kraft-paper, rubber-stamp, condensed-type costume. Dark mode is a neutral charcoal hall, and the laminates in it stay white.
keyCharacteristics: A cool hall-grey ground under a black strap; white laminated badges and credentials that stay white in both themes.
A punched lanyard slot on every laminate, and a punched corner on every ended con.
One variable family, Archivo, set wide (100–125% width) and heavy for names, with tabular numerals everywhere.
Ten flat satin ribbon colours for con types, and they appear only on ribbons.
Ink is the only action colour, and it flips with the theme so it is always the hall's opposite.
Faces on every badge: a strip of photo thumbnails, or dashed empty slots with a plain sentence.
Soft ambient shadows on laminates; flat, hairline-edged pill controls.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink is the only action colour. Every pressed, selected or primary state is a solid ink fill with on-ink text; the one exception is a type ribbon toggle, which presses into its own satin colour. There is no brand accent and no blue link colour.

rules.name: The Ribbon-Only Rule
rules.body: A con-type colour appears only on a satin ribbon or a type ribbon toggle, never as text, icon, border or background anywhere else. The wordmark's CONS in Pop Gold is the single standing exception.

rules.name: The Laminate Rule
rules.body: Badges and credentials keep their printed palette in every theme: Laminate White, Badge Ink at #121418, the light Hairline and Skeleton Grey. Dark mode darkens the hall, the strap and the controls, never a laminate.

rules.name: The Specimen Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size, weight and width, never from colour: headings print in ink, and the ramp is fixed at five sizes (12, 15, 19, 24, 30px) on a 1.25 ratio. The phone search field's 16px exists only to stop iOS from zooming.

rules.name: The Wide Rule
rules.body: Archivo never runs narrower than 100%. Printed labels sit at 104%, small heads at 112%, names at 116%, month heads at 118%, the wordmark at 125%.

rules.name: The Tabular Line Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular everywhere (the body sets them). A date line prints the range on the left and the day count right-aligned in 12px uppercase Pencil Grey, so counts line up down a grid.

rules.name: The Hanging Room Rule
rules.body: Badge grids keep a 54px row gap (50px on phones), because up to three 32px ribbons hang below every badge. Any surface that shows badges leaves that room under them.

rules.name: The Registered Badge Rule
rules.body: Every badge prints the same fields in the same order (art window, name, date line, place line, face strip), with the face strip pinned to the foot, so badges in a row register edge to edge and line for line.

rules.name: The No-Sidebar Rule
rules.body: Filters live in a wrapping row above the content on wide screens and in a bottom sheet on phones, never in a sidebar.

rules.name: The Flat Controls Rule
rules.body: Pills, segments, chips and selects never cast a drop shadow; they are edged with a 1px line (Hairline on the hall, Strap Raised on the strap, an inset 1px ring on the When track). Elevation belongs to laminates and the three popovers: the suggestion panel, the place picker panel and the toast.

rules.name: The Punch Rule
rules.body: A punch is a hole through the laminate to the hall: it takes the ground colour of the current theme and an inset shadow, never a fill of its own.

dos: Do print every con as a badge with its fields in the registered order (art window, name, date line, place line, face strip), with up to three satin ribbons hanging from the bottom edge.
Do give every guest a 4:5 photo credential; when a photo is missing, set their initials on Skeleton Grey. A guest is never a bare name.
Do keep badges and credentials Laminate White with #121418 ink in both themes, and let only the hall, the strap and the controls change with the theme.
Do fill every pressed, selected or primary state with ink and On Ink text; a type ribbon toggle presses into its own satin colour instead.
Do set ribbon labels at 12px, 800, uppercase, in Ribbon White, except Pop (#1d1500) and Horror (#e8d39c), so every label clears 4.5:1.
Do clamp con names at three balanced lines, ellipsise place lines on one line and clamp known-for lines at two, so nothing overflows a laminate.
Do mark an ended con with 72% opacity and the corner punch.
Do show an unannounced lineup as dashed empty photo slots with a plain sentence, never as an empty area.

Do keep a visible 2px focus outline at a 2px offset on everything focusable: ink on the hall and the laminates, Strap Ink on the strap. A hanging ribbon takes an inset 2px ring in its label ink instead, because its notched shape clips anything outside it.
Do collapse every transition and animation to an instant under reduced motion.
donts: Don't add a brand accent, a coloured link or a coloured primary button: ink is the only action colour.
Don't use a ribbon colour for text, icons, borders or backgrounds outside a ribbon or a type toggle; the wordmark's CONS in Pop Gold is the only exception.
Don't mark a place with a map-pin icon; print its country flag (18×13.5px, 2px radius, with a faint hairline ring).
Don't put filters in a sidebar; use the wrapping controls row, and on phones the bottom sheet.
Don't turn dark mode into gamer neon: no glows, no neon tint on the hall or the strap, and never a dark badge or credential.
Don't set Archivo narrower than 100% width or add a second family; condensed type, kraft paper and rubber stamps are rejected looks.
Don't tighten a badge grid's row gap below 54px (50px on phones); the ribbons need that room to hang.
Don't give pills, segments, chips or selects a drop shadow.
Don't add font sizes off the 12/15/19/24/30px ramp; the 16px phone search field is the only exception.
